cases.name: Pivot while preserving identifiers
cases.prompt: A table has patient_id, visit_date, bp_systolic_visit1, bp_systolic_visit2, and weight_visit1. Reshape it to one patient-visit row without accidentally pivoting patient_id or visit_date.
cases.description: Reshape encoded measurement columns while preserving identifier columns and the intended row grain.
traps: Treat missing values as automatically discardable

assertions.text: Uses pivot_longer with explicit measured columns
Parses the encoded names into visit and measure
Preserves patient_id and visit_date as identifiers
Discusses incompatible measures or a .value strategy

cases.name: Resolve duplicate widening keys
cases.prompt: Pivot event data wider by person_id and event_type, but some person/type combinations have multiple timestamps. Explain the correct decision before writing code.
cases.description: Determine whether repeated widening keys represent data quality issues or meaningful repeated events.
traps: Choose mean timestamp without domain justification

assertions.text: Explains that values_fn is needed if aggregation is intended
Distinguishes duplicate data from meaningful repeated events

cases.name: Extract from nested records
cases.prompt: A tibble has a list-column of named API records. Extract status and nested error$message while preserving one row per request, including missing and empty records.
cases.description: Extract selected fields from nested list-columns without changing the request-level row grain.
traps: Fully unnest without considering row grain

assertions.text: Handles missing or empty list elements explicitly
